question.leadin: Answer the following bonus about the colorful history of discrimination in America.
question.text: After World War II, Joseph McCarthy was a leading proponent of the idea that America was being taken over by Communism, a belief often given this two-word name.
question.clue: Mitchell Palmer predicted an uprising on May Day during the first one of these events, in which J. Edgar Hoover organized "raids" which targeted Italian immigrants and anarchists.

swap.text: Clinton's victory in the 1992 election has been linked to this third-party candidate, whose campaign drew voters away from Bush. This billionaire owner of Electronic Data Systems died in 2019.
swap.answerHtml: Ross Perot (accept Henry Ross Perot; accept Henry Ray Perot)
swap.clue: That campaign was hurt by the seeming unpreparedness of this presidential candidate's running mate, who asked "Who am I?" to begin a vice presidential debate; that running mate of his was former Medal of Honor winner James Stockdale.

question.text: The Catholic Knights of Columbus lobbied the Eisenhower administration to add this controversial two-word phrase to the pledge. This phrase has come under fire for seemingly violating the First Amendment.
question.clue: Because John Nicolay and John Hay's drafts omit this phrase, some people are skeptical that this two-word phrase was used before the words "shall have a new birth of freedom" in the last sentence of the Gettysburg Address.

question.text: Francisco Duran shot at who he believed to be this President. He claimed that he was trying to destroy an alien "mist" surrounding the White House that controlled the U.S. Government.
question.clue: He was mocked for giving an overly long nomination speech for Michael Dukakis at the 1988 Democratic National Convention.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about US generals in the twentieth century.
swap.text: When MacArthur was fired, this general was replaced by this general, most well known for reversing the tide in favor of the UN forces.

question.leadin: Identify some candidates from the 1964 U.S. Presidential election.
question.text: Nicknamed "Mr. Conservative," this Republican from Texas became the primary opponent of LBJ, but that's not saying much as he lost a very lopsided election.
question.clue: Ronald Reagan gave his "A Time for Choosing" speech in support of this politician.

question.leadin: Name these people involved in Richard Nixon's "Saturay Night Massacre"
question.text: The first Watergate special prosecutor, he was eventually fired upon demanding Nixon's secret tapes, although Nixon's attorneys general refused to do the deed.

swap.text: Just before the break in, this man invited Davidson to meet with him after hearing rumors Davidson was planning to kidnap him. This National Security Advisor controversially won the 1973 Nobel Peace Prize.
swap.answerHtml: Henry Kissinger [accept Henry Alfred Kissinger; or Heinz Alfred Kissinger]
swap.clue: This man, who may have coordinated the assassination of Archbishop Makarios, coined the term "constructive ambiguity" to describe his policy toward China.

question.answer: read my lips: no new taxes

question.text: All three Apollo 1 crew members previously participated in this second American space program, the successor to Project Mercury. Ed White performed the first American space walk during this program's fourth mission.

question.leadin: Answer the following about people in American history who were revealed as gay or lesbian.
question.text: This former marine intervened to prevent Sara Jane Moore from taking aim for her second shot at Gerald Ford. Afterwards, Harvey Milk outed this man as gay and he was unwittingly lauded as a gay hero by LGBT rights activists.
